reviewer: Claude Code (AI assistant). Not an independent human review.
method: Round two of 1808, under the rule 'every story alike' (11 November 2026): the items that round one held back for framing, counted item by item at the year's rule of 7 newspapers with phrase searches on all 4,466 pages filed under 1808 in both transcriptions, reading of every hit, loose keyword searches of the papers in print without a hit, and scan checks of each admitted passage
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: Governor Sevier's letter from Marble Springs, May 1808
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter of Governor Sevier of Tennessee to a friend at Staunton, Virginia, dated Marble Springs, 14 May 1808, first printed in the Staunton Eagle: an express from General Jackson had reported that '440 Creeks and 12 whites' had taken a position on the south bank of the Tennessee near the mouth of Duck river and had killed about twenty persons; 'If this be true we shall have warm work this summer'. The Eagle adds that two companies of West Tennessee militia were on duty on the frontier. A report at second hand, which the governor passes on with a condition.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

new_groups.label: 'Melancholy Event': Burlington, Vermont, August 1808
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Burlington (Vermont) paragraph of 5 August 1808, headed 'Melancholy Event': a revenue cutter with a lieutenant, a sergeant and twelve privates, sent by the collector of the customs after a large boat 'well known to have been some time employed in smuggling', took her on Onion river; men on the bank then fired on the cutter's crew, and two of the crew and a man of the town were killed. The report says that eight persons were taken and put in gaol, that a jury of inquest found 'wilful murder', and that 'all opinion' should be suspended until the facts were known. A local report.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

new_groups.label: General Wilkinson's challenge to Robert Goodloe Harper, October 1808
new_groups.definition: Printings of notes exchanged at Baltimore on 26 and 27 October 1808, as published there: General James Wilkinson's note to Captain Robert Goodloe Harper, commanding a company of volunteer artillery, charging that Harper had 'secretly assailed the General's honour' and demanding 'the only admissible atonement'; Harper's refusal, which says that his advice to Mr. Clark to lay before Congress documents on Wilkinson's 'connection with the Spanish government' gave no ground for a challenge; and Wilkinson's reply. Each man's own words. The papers print them under their own introductions or headings, such as 'MODERN CHIVALRY' and '"HECTOR" AGAIN.'
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1808 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1808. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. The three items round one left out for framing were read again with phrase searches over all 4,466 pages filed under 1808 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), every hit was read, the papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords (no missed printing), and every printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_13.json and batch_14.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round2.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one: a story needs one printed item found in 7 or more newspapers, counted item by item. All three reach 7 and are admitted as new top-level stories; the parent story of round one on the charges against General Wilkinson names its children in its definition and stays as released.
